outroLine: How many did you get? Thirty or more and you'd pass! Comment your score below, and subscribe with the bell on for a new quiz every day!

lines.q: Barcelona beat PSG six one in 2017. What was the first leg?
lines.a: Four nil to PSG!

lines.q: Only one in ten adults get this right. How long did the Titanic take to sink? Double tap to lock your answer!
lines.a: About two hours and forty minutes! From the iceberg to the end. Follow if you got it!

lines.q: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
lines.a: The Pacific!

lines.q: Quick quiz! Which instrument measures air pressure? Think fast, and lock in your answer.
lines.a: Barometer! A barometer! Meteorologists use air pressure to help track weather.

lines.q: Who made the first successful polio vaccine?
lines.a: Jonas Salk! It was declared safe in nineteen fifty-five.

lines.q: What does a witch traditionally ride?
lines.a: A broomstick!

lines.q: Which nineteen eighty-four film asks: Who you gonna call?
lines.a: Ghostbusters!

lines.q: Quick quiz! What is the largest hot desert in the world? Think fast, and lock in your answer.
lines.a: Sahara! The Sahara! Antarctica is the world's largest desert overall, but it is a polar desert.

lines.q: Which blood type is the universal donor?
lines.a: O negative!

lines.q: In which year did Elvis Presley die?
lines.a: Nineteen seventy-seven!

lines.q: Welcome back, quiz friends! Today: real questions from the U.S. citizenship test. To pass, you need about sixty percent. So, can you get thirty out of fifty? Grab a pen. First one: what is the capital of the United States?
lines.a: Washington, D C! New York was the first capital, under Washington himself.

lines.q: Which British monarch reigned just before Elizabeth the Second?
lines.a: George the Sixth, her father! Edward the Eighth was before him.

lines.q: From which country did the United States buy Alaska?
lines.a: Russia! In eighteen sixty-seven, for about two cents an acre.

lines.q: In which year did World War One begin?
lines.a: Nineteen fourteen!

lines.q: Who was the first woman in space?
lines.a: Valentina Tereshkova! In nineteen sixty-three. Sally Ride came twenty years later.

lines.q: In which year did the Chernobyl disaster happen?
lines.a: Nineteen eighty-six! In Ukraine, then part of the Soviet Union.

lines.q: In which year did the Hindenburg airship disaster happen?
lines.a: Nineteen thirty-seven!

lines.q: Which ballet star defected to the West in nineteen sixty-one?
lines.a: Rudolf Nureyev! At a Paris airport. Baryshnikov followed in seventy-four.

lines.q: Which nineteen sixty-nine music festival was held on a dairy farm in New York State?
lines.a: Woodstock! Over four hundred thousand people came.

lines.q: Which flower decorates Day of the Dead altars?
lines.a: The marigold! Its orange guides the spirits.

lines.q: Quick quiz! Which vitamin can the body produce after sunlight exposure? Think fast, and lock in your answer.
lines.a: Vitamin D! Vitamin D! UVB exposure helps the skin produce it.

lines.q: Only one in ten adults get this right. How long does sunlight take to reach Earth? Double tap to lock your answer!
lines.a: About eight minutes! So you see the Sun as it was eight minutes ago. Follow if you got it!

lines.q: Which animal kills the most people every year?
lines.a: The mosquito! Not the shark. It spreads malaria and other diseases.

lines.q: Who composed the opera The Magic Flute?
lines.a: Mozart! He wrote it in the last year of his life.

lines.q: Quick quiz! What is the smallest prime number? Think fast, and lock in your answer.
lines.a: 2! Two! It is the only even prime number. Follow for another quick quiz.

lines.q: How many players per team are on a football pitch?
lines.a: Eleven!

lines.q: Who was known as the King of Rock and Roll?
lines.a: Elvis Presley!

lines.q: Which band sang Hey Jude?
lines.a: The Beatles! Nineteen sixty-eight.

lines.q: Who wrote Romeo and Juliet?
lines.a: William Shakespeare!

lines.q: Quick quiz! Which blood cells help fight infection? Think fast, and lock in your answer.
lines.a: White blood cells! White blood cells! Different types help the immune system fight infection.

lines.q: How many Earths could fit inside the Sun?
lines.a: About one point three million!

lines.q: Which letter is in no US state name?
lines.a: Q! It's the only one.

lines.q: Which city is home to Big Ben?
lines.a: London! Big Ben is actually the name of the great bell, not the tower.

lines.q: A pumpkin is technically a what?
lines.a: A fruit! It grows from a flower and has seeds.

lines.q: Who wrote the novel Frankenstein?
lines.a: Mary Shelley! She was only a teenager when she began it.

lines.q: Who was Britain's prime minister for most of World War Two?
lines.a: Winston Churchill!

lines.q: Which city hosted the nineteen sixty-eight Summer Olympics?
lines.a: Mexico City! The first Games in Latin America.

lines.q: In which year was the Battle of Hastings?
lines.a: Ten sixty-six! William the Conqueror won the crown of England.

lines.q: How many strings does a violin have?
lines.a: Four! Okay, warm-up done. Now it gets harder.

lines.q: Which amendment ended slavery?
lines.a: The thirteenth! In eighteen sixty-five.

lines.q: Three left, stay with me! Who was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic?
lines.a: Amelia Earhart! In nineteen thirty-two.

lines.q: Now it gets really tough. Who sang A Whiter Shade of Pale in nineteen sixty-seven?
lines.a: Procol Harum! That organ line is unforgettable.

lines.q: Which planet has the most known moons?
lines.a: Saturn! Over two hundred and seventy.

lines.q: Which US state grows the most pumpkins?
lines.a: Illinois! By far.

lines.q: Which country has the most people today?
lines.a: India! It passed China in twenty twenty-three.

lines.q: A group of crows is called a what?
lines.a: A murder! Spooky, right?

lines.q: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
lines.a: Leonardo da Vinci!

lines.q: Who scored the first ever Premier League goal?
lines.a: Brian Deane! For Sheffield United.

lines.q: How many stars are on the U.S. flag?
lines.a: Fifty! One for every state. The last two were added in nineteen sixty.

lines.q: The Federalist Papers argued in favour of what?
lines.a: Passing the U.S. Constitution! Eighty-five essays in New York newspapers.
